claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC dendritic alloy without oxide dispersoids.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 800 MPa at low temperature.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Nano-scale Y2O3 particles can be incorporated into TiVNbTa through an oxide-dispersion-strengthening powder-metallurgy route.
The intervention will produce a high density of uniformly dispersed nano-scale Y2O3 particles in the BCC matrix.
Dispersed nano-oxides act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles act as grain-boundary pinning sites in TiVNbTa.
The proposed strengthening includes an Orowan-type mechanism.
Y2O3 dispersoids will inhibit grain coarsening in TiVNbTa at high temperature.
Y2O3 dispersoids will inhibit dynamic recovery in TiVNbTa at high temperature.
Dispersion strengthening can contribute to the strength of high-entropy alloys.
Adding nano-scale Y2O3 will mitigate high-temperature softening of TiVNbTa.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will retain a yield strength above the 330 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The strengthened alloy may approach its lower-temperature strength without a drastic loss of ductility.
The magnitude of elevated-temperature strength improvement will depend on dispersion quality, particle-matrix interfaces, and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires Y2O3 particles as a distinct dispersed phase while also saying the process should maintain a single-phase BCC structure. This is contradictory unless 'single-phase' is explicitly restricted to the metallic matrix.
